Let v(t) denote the speed of a car at time t (in hours) since the car started its journey. The graph of y=v′(t), the derivative of v(t), is given above. Find all the values of t where the speed of a car is decreasing.

a
t∈(0,2)
b
t∈(7,8)
c
t∈(0,2)∪(5,8]
d
t∈(2,4)∪(6,8]
e
t∈(0,2)∪(4,6)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the following:

  • If v′(t)=0 for all t∈(a,b), then v(t) is constant on (a,b).

  • When v′(t)>0 for all t∈(a,b), then v(t) is increasing on (a,b).

  • When v′(t)<0 for all t∈(a,b), then v(t) is decreasing on (a,b).

From the above graph, we can see that v′(t) is negative on the intervals (2,4) and (6,8]:

Therefore, the speed of a car is decreasing when t∈(2,4)∪(6,8].
